## Overview

Enable batch-invariant Qwen GatedDeltaNet prefill, cached continuation and decode under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` by sharing recurrent arithmetic. Supersedes #49827 and addresses the prefill-partitioning concerns in #48613. AI assistance was used.

## Claims

- Non-speculative Qwen GDN tokens use the existing recurrent kernel in BIC mode, instead of switching arithmetic between chunked prefill and recurrent decode.
- Exact output and persistent-state checks pass across the tested prefill partitions and decode replay. The existing public Qwen online BS1-vs-BSN token/logprob test passes.
- The non-BIC numerical route is unchanged. Speculative decoding is explicitly unsupported; this is a correctness feature with a measured performance cost, not a speedup.

The diff is reduced from +421/-25 to **+205/-22 including tests**. The bespoke HTTP test and overlapping mock-heavy test were removed; the existing online suite and exact partition/state regression remain. This is still above the reviewer's ideal 200-line size.

## Validation

Tested head **`1cdaeab837`**, based on upstream main snapshot **`11a8d571d2`**, on 22 October. This is not a claim about a later main revision.

H100, public `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, TP1, BF16, eager MRV1, FLASH_ATTN, prefix cache off. Base and PR use matching dependencies: torch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, transformers 5.20.2 and lm_eval 0.4.13. Wheel `a6c898e2a` has identical native build inputs and CUDA/common requirements to the pinned base. Remote source checks after validation match the pushed patch.

**[Exact commands and native output, including all 18 serving measurements](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60033#issuecomment-6345622498).** The summaries below do not replace those raw outputs.

### Correctness

The same existing online Qwen test fails on the base snapshot with `RuntimeError: VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for GDN_ATTN.` and passes on this PR: 1 passed, 2 deselected. The base error establishes the unsupported gate, not a numeric failure of an enabled base kernel.

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
export VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B
export VLLM_TEST_SERVER_ARGS='--max-num-batched-tokens 128 --enforce-eager --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 --no-enable-prefix-caching'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/determinism/test_online_batch_invariance.py \
  -k 'bs1_vs_bsN and FLASH_ATTN' -v -s --tb=short
```

Additional regressions: 10 kernel tests, 1 compiler/cache-key test and 11 NIXL state-layout tests passed. Partition tests compare output, convolution state and recurrent state exactly, including state reload. Applicable pre-commit checks, including mypy and CI test tethering, passed on the same source.

The online test checks output tokens and selected-token logprobs; it is not full-vocabulary logit-hash validation. Older cache-on/compiled/4B experiments from the previous head are not substituted for this head's evidence.

### Accuracy

Full five-shot GSM8K via `lm_eval`: all 1,319 questions in base-normal and PR-BIC modes, seed 42, greedy generation capped at 256 tokens, concurrency eight. Document, prompt and target hashes match across modes, with complete nonempty responses.

- Flexible-extract exact match: base normal 451/1319 (34.19%), PR BIC 455/1319 (34.50%).
- Strict-match exact match: base normal 449/1319 (34.04%), PR BIC 451/1319 (34.19%).

No observed aggregate accuracy drop on this run, not statistical equivalence or broad quality validation. Generated text differs on 417 questions; BIC is not expected to reproduce ordinary batch-variable arithmetic.

### Serving Performance

Unprofiled `vllm bench serve`, three fresh-server rounds each for base normal, PR normal and PR BIC, alternating mode order. Concurrency eight, scheduling token budget 128, four warmups, seed 42, fixed lengths and forced output length. All 18 runs passed equal-work checks. Artifact uploads occurred outside measured benchmark commands.

- Prefill-heavy: 128 requests at 1024 input / 1 output token. Median request/s: base normal 3.393, PR normal 3.317, PR BIC 2.883. BIC is 15.0% below base normal, or 13.1% below PR normal.
- Mixed: 64 requests at 1024 input / 128 output tokens. Median request/s: base normal 1.614, PR normal 1.583, PR BIC 1.299. BIC is 19.5% below base normal, or 17.9% below PR normal.

This measures the combined BIC cost, including global GEMM behavior, not GDN-only overhead. Three repetitions are not a significance test; all repetition results and native TTFT/TPOT/ITL output are in the linked comment. Accuracy-run duration is not used as throughput evidence.

## Details

### Why Shared Recurrence

Chunked prefill and recurrent decode implement the same mathematical operation but can produce different floating-point results. Scheduler batching and prefill partitioning can therefore change a request's output. Opening the backend support flag alone does not resolve that.

In BIC mode this change shares recurrent arithmetic across non-speculative Qwen GDN prefill, continuation and decode, preserving convolution/recurrent state across arbitrary tested partitions. It also adds a Qwen-specific backend identity/support gate, includes the Inductor BIC policy in the compilation cache configuration, and makes normalization row tiling independent of batch size. XPU/NIXL references account for the backend identity. No scheduler chunk-grid restriction is added.

### Related Work And Open Review Points

- #57280 addresses normalization row tiling. This PR includes overlapping policy needed by the tested path; that overlap needs resolving before merge.
- #45819 opens GDN batch-invariance support. This PR additionally shares arithmetic between prefill and decode.
- #55868 aligns prefill/cache chunk grids; this approach instead shares recurrence across arbitrary tested partitions.
- #62343 uses recurrence for short prefills with a batch-dependent threshold. It references this PR but does not replace its invariant routing policy.
- The `QWEN_GDN_ATTN` versus `GDN_ATTN` naming is under review following @ZJY0516's comment; no naming change has been made yet.

### Out Of Scope And Limits

TP/EP, MRV2, Blackwell, multi-node, prefix-cache-on serving and live disaggregated state transfer are not validated by this matrix. Speculative decoding is unsupported. Long prefills may be slower under the recurrent route.

GEMM performance (#60034) and TP collective work (#50299) remain separate follow-ups; they do not establish multi-GPU correctness for this PR. No universal determinism or merge readiness is claimed.

Local validation does not replace upstream CI. Older Intel failures discussed in the thread belong to earlier heads; this update does not claim to fix or clear them, and no unrelated CI repairs are bundled here.

detail.body:
## Overview

Enable batch-invariant Qwen GatedDeltaNet prefill, cached continuation and decode under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` by sharing recurrent arithmetic. Supersedes #49827 and addresses the prefill-partitioning concerns in #48613. AI assistance was used.

## Claims

- Non-speculative Qwen GDN tokens use the existing recurrent kernel in BIC mode, instead of switching arithmetic between chunked prefill and recurrent decode.
- Exact output and persistent-state checks pass across the tested prefill partitions and decode replay. The existing public Qwen online BS1-vs-BSN token/logprob test passes.
- The non-BIC numerical route is unchanged. Speculative decoding is explicitly unsupported; this is a correctness feature with a measured performance cost, not a speedup.

### Accuracy

Full five-shot GSM8K via `lm_eval`: all 1,319 questions in base-normal and PR-BIC modes, seed 42, greedy generation capped at 256 tokens, concurrency eight. Document, prompt and target hashes match across modes, with complete nonempty responses.

- Flexible-extract exact match: base normal 451/1319 (34.19%), PR BIC 455/1319 (34.50%).
- Strict-match exact match: base normal 449/1319 (34.04%), PR BIC 451/1319 (34.19%).

### Serving Performance

Unprofiled `vllm bench serve`, three fresh-server rounds each for base normal, PR normal and PR BIC, alternating mode order. Concurrency eight, scheduling token budget 128, four warmups, seed 42, fixed lengths and forced output length. All 18 runs passed equal-work checks. This measures the combined BIC cost, including global GEMM behavior, not GDN-only overhead. Three repetitions are not a significance test; all repetition results and native TTFT/TPOT/ITL output are in the linked comment. Accuracy-run duration is not used as throughput evidence.

## Details

### Why Shared Recurrence

Chunked prefill and recurrent decode implement the same mathematical operation but can produce different floating-point results. Scheduler batching and prefill partitioning can therefore change a request's output. Opening the backend support flag alone does not resolve that.

In BIC mode this change shares recurrent arithmetic across non-speculative Qwen GDN prefill, continuation and decode, preserving convolution/recurrent state across arbitrary tested partitions. It also adds a Qwen-specific backend identity/support gate, includes the Inductor BIC policy in the compilation cache configuration, and makes normalization row tiling independent of batch size. XPU/NIXL references account for the backend identity. No scheduler chunk-grid restriction is added.

### Related Work And Open Review Points

- #57280 addresses normalization row tiling. This PR includes overlapping policy needed by the tested path; that overlap needs resolving before merge.
- #45819 opens GDN batch-invariance support. This PR additionally shares arithmetic between prefill and decode.
- #55868 aligns prefill/cache chunk grids; this approach instead shares recurrence across arbitrary tested partitions.
- #62343 uses recurrence for short prefills with a batch-dependent threshold. It references this PR but does not replace its invariant routing policy.
- The `QWEN_GDN_ATTN` versus `GDN_ATTN` naming is under review following @ZJY0516's comment; no naming change has been made yet.

### Out Of Scope And Limits

TP/EP, MRV2, Blackwell, multi-node, prefix-cache-on serving and live disaggregated state transfer are not validated by this matrix. Speculative decoding is unsupported. Long prefills may be slower under the recurrent route.

GEMM performance (#60034) and TP collective work (#50299) remain separate follow-ups; they do not establish multi-GPU correctness for this PR. No universal determinism or merge readiness is claimed.
